threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for your coffee ‘to go’ instead of embracing the sit-and-savor vibe at the local cafés.
Heard a couple arguing about whether the chips from the late-night fish shop were worth the wait. She swore by the tartar sauce – typical Brixton debate!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids playing football in the street while the baker yelled to them to watch out for her croissants. Felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's normal to have outdoor screenings of obscure films right in the middle of the street. You catch a classic while sipping on a Berliner Weiße. Truly unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they gossip about the BART delays—it's practically a weather report these days. Newbies just look confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a guy serenaded the whole 19 bus with a ukulele. We all forgot about the delays and just sang along. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about bars and restaurants, but many miss the community art projects tucked between the façades.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still pull out a map instead of using their phone for directions—makes them stand out in Gràcia's winding streets.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it’s called ‘the Overground’ instead of just ‘Overground’. That subtle shift makes all the difference.
Caught two blokes arguing over whether a double cheeseburger beats a chicken nugget meal. They settled it with a dance-off on the bus aisle.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught a late-night kebab near Hermannplatz, saw a pack of wild cats lounging under the neon lights like they owned the place. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you sip beer in a park while watching an impromptu DJ set from a guy on a bicycle. It’s like street culture on wheels!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name the bus that’s always late but still depend on it for life. It’s like a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy casually juggling while waiting for the 19 to show up—Muni’s delays turn us all into street performers, I guess.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think the fountains at Plaça del Sol are for splashing around; locals know they’re just the backdrop for a quiet evening with a beer.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their oversized map folded awkwardly in hand while they stare at the street signs, trying to decipher the Catalan names.
